title: Initial Experiences with DAOS Object Storage on Aurora
problem: Understanding how hardware topology, network concurrency, and I/O API choices impact real-world I/O performance on the DAOS-based Aurora storage platform. The unique combination of NVMe drives, persistent memory, storage servers, and RDMA network fabric presents unclear optimal configuration parameters.
motivation: Aurora offers unprecedented I/O performance potential (230 PiB capacity, 31 TiB/s throughput), but practitioners need empirical guidance to extract maximum effective performance from this class of storage system.
method: The researchers tested a small-scale DAOS storage system (which combines NVMe drives, persistent memory, storage servers, and RDMA—a fast network technology) by systematically changing different settings. They varied the physical arrangement of hardware (topology), how many network requests could happen at the same time (concurrency), and which input/output API programs used to access data. They measured how fast data actually moved under each configuration to see which choices had the biggest impact on real-world performance.
key_novelty: DAOS storage performance on Aurora depends on how hardware topology, network concurrency (parallel operations), and I/O API design interact with each other.
contributions: Initial empirical characterization of DAOS on Aurora storage platform
Sensitivity analysis of I/O performance to hardware topology parameters
Sensitivity analysis of I/O performance to network concurrency
Recommendations for optimizing performance on DAOS-based storage systems
limitations: Study limited to small-scale characterization; results may not generalize beyond Aurora's specific hardware configuration.
primary_theme: I/O performance characterization of distributed storage
